Name: Shiver
Notes: Directed by Grant Gee, who also made Meeting People Is Easy, the Shiver music video features Coldplay performing in a studio. The spinning globe from the Parachutes cover sits atop an amplifier—purchased by Chris Martin for £10 at WHSmith. The globe later appeared in animated form in Don't Panic and traveled with the band on the Parachutes World Tour.

Name: Yellow
Notes: The video is a single continuous shot of Chris Martin walking alone on a rainy beach in England. Originally, the plan featured the full band on a sunny beach with extras, but after drummer Will Champion’s mother passed away, the other members attended her funeral. With the crew already in place, Martin filmed the video solo. The entire album, Parachutes, is dedicated to Will’s mother, Sara.

Name: Trouble (UK Version)

Name: Trouble (US Version)
Notes: The video embraces the "Don't Panic" motif with a unique two-dimensional cut-out style. It follows the band riding a horse-drawn carriage through a forest, while a woman tends to plants atop a mountain. A small crow from the carriage transforms into a dark cloud, bringing rain that leaves eerie holes and crow feathers in its wake. Ultimately, a tornado relocates the woman’s house to a suburban setting, blending surrealism with symbolism.

Name: Don't Panic
Notes: Directed by British animator Tim Hope, the Don't Panic music video presents the band as two-dimensional paper cutouts performing household chores. Chaos ensues as floods overtake their home and village, forcing them to escape by boat. The video concludes with an animated take on the iconic yellow globe from Parachutes.

Name: The Scientist
Notes: Directed by Jamie Thraves, it starts with Chris Martin lying on a mattress and plays in reverse as we see how he got there. We learn that he was driving on a country road with his girlfriend in the passenger's seat when he swerved to avoid another vehicle, sending their car careening down a hill. His girlfriend is tossed through the windshield and presumably dead, but Martin wakes up and wanders off, eventually ending up on the mattress. Chris Martin had to learn how  to sing the song backwards for the video.

Name: Clocks
Notes: The video was directed by Dominic Leung and shot at ExCeL London. It shows the band performing with a light show in front of an audience made up of local college students. On his left hand, Martin has handwritten the words "MakeTradeFair.com." The website, which shut down in 2004, was part of a campaign organized by Oxfam calling for fair trade policies.
